stem:
Meera connects a cell, a lamp and a switch in series to check her science project at home, as shown in the figure.

When the switch is in the position shown, what happens to the lamp?

options.text: The lamp glows, because the switch itself supplies current to the lamp.
The lamp glows, because the switch has closed the gap and completed the circuit.
The lamp stays off, because the open switch has broken the path of the circuit.
The lamp stays off, because a cell can never light a lamp without a switch.

teacher.key_rationale: The figure shows an open (normally open) switch, so the circuit path is broken and no current flows; the lamp stays off. Option C states this correctly. Option A is the trap for students who think the switch supplies current; B wrongly treats the shown open switch as closed; D is a false general claim.
teacher.figure_note: Single circuitikz figure: cell, lamp and open switch in series; switch shown open.
